description:
FILED s464ax from the #985 probe battery (50 slice shapes vs perl 5.40.3).
PRE-EXISTING â reproduces on main `80b715c`.

    my @a = (10,20,30,40,50);
    print join(',', %a[-1]),     "\n";   # perl -1,50      PCL 4,50
    print join(',', %a[-2,-1]),  "\n";   # perl -2,40,-1,50  PCL 3,40,4,50
    my $r = \@a;
    print join(',', %{$r}[-1]),  "\n";   # perl -1,50      PCL 4,50
    print join(',', %a[1]),      "\n";   # perl 1,20       PCL 1,20   (agree)

perl's `pp_kvaslice` pushes the SUBSCRIPT the program wrote as the key half
and the element as the value half; it does not report the normalised index.
PCL's `p-kv-aslice` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) computes

    (i (truncate (to-number idx)))
    (i (if (< i 0) (max 0 (+ (length arr) i)) i))

and then boxes THAT `i` as the key half, so the normalisation leaks into the
returned key.  The normalised index is still needed for the VALUE half.

FIX SHAPE: keep the normalised index for `%p-alias-aelem` and box the
ORIGINAL subscript for the key half.  Watch the exact spelling perl emits for
a non-integer or string subscript (`%a["-1"]`, `%a[1.7]`) before choosing
between "the argument as given" and "truncate(to-number(arg))" â probe it.

Also probe what `%a[-1]` does when the element is then ALIASED through a sub
call: the s464ax battery saw `-1,U` from `d(%a[-1])` where a direct `join`
gave `-1,50`, i.e. perl's own answer differs between the two consumers.  That
may be a second finding or may be #1010's vivification rule in the array
family; measure before assuming.

SIZE: small.  op/kvaslice.t is the companion file that would move (it is
DIFF today, and 25 of its rows are currently blessed against #930).  A filler.
subject: A KV array slice `%a[-1]` returns the index AS WRITTEN in perl; PCL normalises it to the positive index
